findings.fix: Remove the install hook or reduce it to a plain build step. Nothing at install time should read the environment or talk to the network.
findings.title: Install script reads secrets and opens network connections
findings.description: The repo's own install script (postinstall) reads secrets and opens network connections. It reads the whole environment (where API keys and tokens live) and makes network connections, the pattern of install-time credential theft. This audit let it run inside the sandbox; the containment log shows what it tried.

findings.fix: Check package.json scripts (preinstall/install/postinstall/prepare, build) and each dependency's install scripts for network calls; remove the code or the dependency. Install with --ignore-scripts until you have.
findings.title: Install-time code opened a direct network connection
findings.description: During install, code from the repo or one of its dependencies tried to reach tcp 192.0.2.1:443, tcp 169.254.169.254:80, tcp 172.30.0.1:2375, tcp 172.30.0.1:22 without going through the egress proxy it was given. The sandbox firewall dropped it, so nothing left; on a developer laptop or a CI runner it would have. Package managers and legitimate download scripts honour the proxy, so a raw connection like this is deliberate: treat the repo as hostile until you know what made it.
